errors.evidence: The chart clearly displays four main layers in the inner ring: Perception Layer (40.4%), Semantic Layer (41.2%), Cultural Layer (14.1%), and Signal Layer (4.3%). The description incorrectly states there are three.
The chart does not contain 17 slices. The inner ring has 4 slices (layers), and the outer ring has 16 slices (subcategories). The total number of distinct segments is 20.
The chart shows "Music Theory" and "Counting & Statistics" as two separate slices in the outer ring. The description incorrectly combines them into a single category.

errors.text_span: with darker shades representing larger proportions
errors.evidence: This statement is false. The largest category, "Semantic Layer" (41.2%), is a lighter shade of blue than the second-largest category, "Perception Layer" (40.4%), which is dark blue.

errors.text_span: Some slices are further divided into subcategories.
errors.evidence: This misrepresents the chart's structure. It is a two-level chart where all four inner slices (layers) are divided into subcategories in the outer ring, it is not the case that only 'some' are.

errors.text_span: The three main layers are labeled and include percentage values: Signal Layer (4.3%), Semantic Layer (41.2%), and Perception Layer (40.4%), while the Cultural Layer is also labeled with a percentage (14.1%).
errors.evidence: This sentence is contradictory and confusing. It begins by stating there are three main layers and lists them, but then introduces the fourth layer ("Cultural Layer") as an afterthought, which is a result of the initial error of miscounting the layers.
